What do you want to see?

Only the user journey is the real step-by-step flow. The other options are reference sections; on the map they have dashed borders and a 📚 tag.

New here? Start with this · about 2 minutes

What is EDU 360?

🎓 In one line

EDU 360 is one web app that runs universities, colleges and schools in one place: students, teachers and staff, classes, attendance, exams and results, fees, leave, messages and reports. It works in the browser on phones, tablets and computers. The first release is for India, in English.

🏢 Who is who: the levels

🛠 Platform teamruns EDU 360💼 Tenantthe paying customer🏛 University🏫 College / School📚 Department / Class👩‍🏫 Teachers · 🧑‍🎓 Students · 👪 Parents

A tenant is one customer: a university with all its colleges and schools, or one standalone college, or one standalone school. Each tenant's data is kept separate. The platform team runs the product and the billing but never sees a tenant's student, staff or money data.

👤 Roles: who can see what

Everyone logs in as one of 71 roles, such as Principal, Teacher, Accountant or Parent. After logging in they land on their own home screen, and see only what their role and scope allow. A teacher sees only their own classes, a parent only their own child, and a Principal the whole college.

What a role may do in each area is shown with letters: F Full · M Manage · C Configure · A Approve · V View · R Request · N No access. Underneath are 278 exact actions, such as "Mark attendance" or "Publish results", and every one is checked by the system.

✅ Approvals

Important requests (leave, marks, fees, results, notices and more) go through an approval chain: a fixed order of approvers. There are 60 chains. The rules are the same everywhere:

  • Each approver can only approve or reject. A rejection needs a remark and ends the request; the person can submit again.
  • Nobody approves their own request.
  • Requests never approve themselves; the system only sends reminders.

🧑‍🎓 Students and parents

School: students normally don't log in; their parent does. A school can switch on login for chosen classes (for example 9–12), with a limited view. College: students and parents both log in, each with their own account.

🧩 29 modules, in phases

The product is split into modules such as Users & access, Attendance, Exams, Fees, Leave and Communication. Phase 1 launches first. Phase 2 modules (such as payroll, admissions, library and placement) and Phase 3 modules come later. On the map, Phase 2 boxes are purple and Phase 3 boxes have dashed borders.

🔒 Safety built in

Sensitive roles need a two-step code after the password. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes. Every important action is written to an audit log that can't be edited.

🗺 How to use this map

Start with Follow the user journey (the real flow), or Log in as a role to see one person's day. Tap any box to read what happens, in plain words. Use ▶ Walk to go one box at a time.

EDU 360 V4.0 · UI/UX

UI/UX screen-state contract and audit

EDU 360 V4.0 · Deliverable 7. Status 30 Oct 2026: released with the V4.0 set. This page is a visual aid to Deliverable 1 (Master Product Specification); where they differ, Deliverable 1 wins [C1].

1. States every screen must have

Loading (skeleton) · empty (with the next useful action) · validation error (summary + field messages) · server error (with correlation ID, never stack traces) · permission denied ("You don't have access to this" and an audit event) · read-only (trial ended, locked term or month, published or decided record) · success (toast + new state visible). Every action button is shown only when the Action List allows it and is still re-checked by the server.

2a. Roles and permissions screens (V4.0)

Specified in Deliverable 3, sheet Roles & Permissions Screens: RP-01 Roles · RP-02 Role detail · RP-03 Create / edit custom role · RP-04 Assign roles · RP-05 User access · RP-06 Missing roles (roll-down) · RP-07 Delegations · RP-08 Access review and role audit. Standard roles are read-only; custom roles use Action List actions only; IT roles see non-sensitive roles only; nobody changes their own roles. On RP-06, unresolved rows come first; a change needs a reason; an approval can be moved but never withheld. Any decision taken through roll-down carries the "Acting for …" badge (Deliverable 9).

GuardNameRule
RD-G1No self-approvalA stand-in never decides their own request; the step goes to the next stand-in, else the level above [D-002].
RD-G2Preparer is never the approverIf roll-down makes the preparer of an item also its approver, the approval goes to the next stand-in, else the level above [AP-04, C3].
RD-G3Two steps on one person collapseIf two consecutive steps of one chain land on the same person, that person decides once; the step is recorded as COLLAPSED (V3.3: "one Principal approval is enough" [R2-03]).
RD-G4Own-leave approvers never roll downThe Principal's, Vice-Chancellor's and Data Protection Contact's own leave keep their named approver (Management or Governing Body Approver); the go-live gate is unchanged [C6, C7, V4-DB-01].
RD-G5Never to personal or platform rolesStudents, parents, applicants, the Governing Body Approver and platform roles are never stand-ins; roll-down never crosses an institution or tenant boundary.
RD-G6Limits of the stand-in stayIT roles still assign non-sensitive roles only [MX-04]; a stand-in using a sensitive action must use two-step login; separation-of-duties pairs (Deliverable 3) still apply.
RD-G7Always visible and loggedEvery action taken through roll-down records "acting for <role>" (approval_step.acting_for_role, audit entry) and the screen shows an "Acting for …" badge.
RD-G8Authority returns automaticallyWhen someone is appointed to the missing role, new items go to them; pending approvals move to them and the Admin is warned [WF-26].

3. Design system and prototype (V4.0 status)

  • Deliverable 9 — Master Design System v2.1 (V4.0 edition): no "Return for changes" on approvals; attendance statuses P / A / On approved leave / Not held; 52 text–background token pairs measured, all WCAG 2.2 AA.
  • Deliverable 10 — Interactive Prototype V4.0: 8 personas including the Governing Body Approver; parent online payment; notice publishing; decision register reconciled with V3.3 (21 resolved, 4 open: DR-19 to DR-22).
  • Fonts must be self-hosted in the product (privacy, CSP).

4. Accessibility target

WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every page, state and breakpoint; keyboard paths for every action; visible focus; status messages announced; no colour-only meaning.

C1 UI/UX and design audit (carried forward in full)

Status: source-structure and design-token inventory expanded; interaction-by-interaction browser audit remains outstanding. This is not a certification of implemented functionality or accessibility conformance.

1. Source assets and structural coverage

  • Interactive Prototype V3.3: 1,904 source lines; 100 unique static IDs; 226 CSS classes; 13 static <button> tags; 8 static <form> tags. Some controls are generated dynamically by script, so static HTML counts are not a control count or proof of interaction.
  • Master Design System v2.1: 3,319 source lines; 344 static IDs; 92 buttons; 3 forms; 287 unique CSS classes; 211 unique CSS custom properties across 290 declarations.
  • Unified Master Flow: complete uploaded 1.9 MB HTML source retained in the V4.0 interactive source file, with a banner explaining its original V3.2 metadata and a separate updated V4.0 workflow index.
  • The 0/92 button or 0/form claims from earlier drafts were inaccurate for the design system; the counts above are measured from the actual HTML files.

2. Design-system governance and foundations

  • System name: Stillwater. Token tiers: primitives, semantic tokens, then component tokens; use a single canonical token block. Components must consume semantic/component tokens rather than ad hoc primitive values.
  • Typography families: DM Sans for body/UI; Manrope for display/headings; Noto Sans Devanagari and Noto Sans Kannada as Indic fallbacks; monospace for code/identifiers.
  • Supported visual directions: light and dark theme variables. Dark theme is marked beta in the source; do not assume production dark-theme readiness without contrast and state testing.
  • Principles explicitly in the design-system headings: calm/trustworthy; task-first; explain state; context always visible; accessible by default; consequences before commitment.
  • Component families explicitly in the source headings include buttons, form fields, choice controls, status badges/tags/chips, notices/banners/toasts, tooltips, dialogs/drawers, navigation/breadcrumbs/tabs/pagination/overflow menus, data display/tables, KPI cards, avatars/identity, timeline, accordion, stepper, progress/loading/empty states and charts.

6. Role-aware UI contract

  1. Resolve the authenticated identity and exactly one active role assignment/scope before loading protected data.
  2. Navigation and controls reflect module entitlements and allowed action codes, but hiding a control is not a security boundary.
  3. All protected requests are re-authorized on the server against tenant, institution, assignment, active role, action code, field sensitivity, record state and approval-chain position.
  4. Approval controls are available only to the eligible current chain actor; reject requires the required remark; no self-approval or duplicate chain actor is allowed.
  5. Context switching invalidates/refetches page data. Results must not union separate assignments unless a specifically authorized cross-scope action exists.
  6. Sensitive read/export/correct/delete actions must be separately authorized and audited. Error states must not reveal cross-tenant object existence.

7. Screen/state reconciliation matrix

Area Screens/states to validate Relevant action/API/data families
Sign-in & identity login, OTP, MFA, first-login reset, device management, session expiry, lockout, invalid credentials AUTH_*; identity-event API; user/device/audit entities
Users & roles user list/detail, create/edit, assignment, active-context switch, template selector, custom role editor, lifecycle, denied scope USER_/ROLE_; users/roles/me APIs; user/role assignment tables
Institution setup tenant, university/institution, departments, programs, semesters, classes, sections, activation gates institution setup actions; institution RLS/go-live
Timetable slot builder, clash view, allocations, publication, syllabus, substitute assignment TIMETABLE/SYLLABUS; timetable APIs/tables
Attendance session marking, NOT_HELD, offline draft/sync conflict, correction request, approval/lock states ATTENDANCE_*; attendance APIs/tables; OD-04/OD-07
Exams & results exam pattern, schedule, hall ticket, marks submission, result publish/withdraw, blocked re-evaluation EXAM/RESULT; exam/result APIs and entities
Fees fee structure draft/submit/approve/live, installments, payment intent, gateway callback, receipt, ledger, credit FE_*; fees/payment/webhook APIs and ledger entities
Leave application, attachments, eligibility, chain, delegation, reject/resubmit, approver configuration leave actions; approval APIs/chains; go-live blocker
Communication notice/message/event composer, audience, publish, delivery status, read/acknowledge COMMUNICATION/COMMUNITY actions and delivery entities
Reports report filter, scope preview, export, async status, empty/denied/too-large states REPORTS actions/APIs; export job and audit
Governance & privacy complaints, sensitive notes, policy/docs, legal holds, privacy requests, incidents, data exports GOVERNANCE/DATA actions; retention/audit/legal-hold entities
Platform/support tenant lifecycle, subscription and entitlements, support ticket access grant, release/feature controls PLATFORM actions; platform APIs; support grants/entitlements

8. Template-selection UI contract (V4.0 recommendation)

  1. Administrator selects organisational level and one of the standard baseline templates.
  2. UI prepopulates the draft with the source-derived role/action profile and functional-area letters. It does not assign a user or activate the role.
  3. UI displays the permission legend, per-action scope, sensitive-data classification, Never allowed rules and approval authority boundaries.
  4. Editable actions are limited by the creator’s own authority and delegated scope; platform-reserved and approval-chain controls remain protected.
  5. Save/activate role and assign to user are separate operations; both create audit events and permission diffs.
  6. Role permission changes trigger impact preview and revalidation of all existing assignments.

9. Accessibility and responsive behaviour

  • Preserve 44px target guidance from the design-system tokens. Do not infer WCAG conformance merely from target size.
  • The token inventory includes a dedicated focus color/ring and component sizing guidance. Every keyboard path must remain visible and operable.
  • Validate labels/descriptions/errors, live announcements for async changes, modal focus trapping/restoration, skip navigation, data-table semantics, zoom/reflow, reduced motion and dark-theme contrast.
  • Target WCAG 2.2 AA as a V4.0 QA recommendation. Conformance is unverified until automated and manual audit evidence is available.

10. Outstanding audit work and evidence limits

  • No complete browser click-through of every prototype interaction/state was executed in this repair.
  • Prototype element IDs and CSS classes are source inventory only; generated screens/controls may not be visible in static HTML.
  • No screen-by-screen review against all 2,874 API/DB field-map rows was completed.
  • API operations and database entities are documented; no live frontend/backend runtime was provided.
  • Full V4.0 prototype changes beyond the workflow source banner/index are not claimed. The original prototype and design system remain preserved as separate source files.
EDU 360 V4.0

What changed in this map in V4.0

EDU 360 V4.0 · Deliverable 7. Status 30 Oct 2026: released with the V4.0 set. This page is a visual aid to Deliverable 1 (Master Product Specification); where they differ, Deliverable 1 wins [C1].

  • Role roll-down (decision V4-PD-01, 30 Oct 2026): when a level or role is missing, its approvals go to the head of the next level down and its other actions to the admin; the level above can change this. A standalone college or school is activated by its Principal acting for the Vice-Chancellor. New journey WF-V4-13; screens RP-01 to RP-08.
  • Rules: the map now follows the V3.3 rules (Deliverable 1, Part II): 71 roles, 278 actions (Action List V3.3), the Role × Action grid of V3.3 for every role's action boxes, V3.3 matrix letters, and the V3.3 workflow tables of Sections 11–14 with a "Changed in 3.3" box wherever V3.3 added a rule to a role.
  • Governing Body Approver (C6, C13): new role journey — login with two-step code, a dashboard that shows only pending leave for which it is the approver, approve / reject the Principal's, the Vice-Chancellor's or a dedicated Data Protection Contact's own leave.
  • Approval chains: V3.3 rows added (Data Protection Contact's own leave, policy in a standalone institution, compliance reports and statutory returns, accreditation items, go-live) and changed rows updated; the Principal's-leave step now names the Governing Body Approver and the V4.0 rule that the approver is never the Principal.
  • Full document: "Master Document V3.2" replaced by "Master Document V3.3" — every section of Deliverable 1, Part II.
  • Counts: all V3.2 counts (70 roles, 270 actions, 55 chains, 1,782 role–action pairs, 563 steps) replaced by the V3.3 values computed from the sources.
  • Authority: this map is a visual aid. Where it differs from Deliverable 1, 2 or 3, those win [C1].
  • Evidence: the page was loaded and clicked in Chromium after the update (Deliverable 8, UI checks); every edge points to an existing box.

How to read this map

  1. From START, the green ▶ Open portal line is the real flow. Dashed 📚 lines lead to reference sections (roles, chains, modules, the document); they are not flow steps. 🏠 Start lets you choose one.
  2. Tap a box to read its full text. Tap ⤢ to open it as a big popup.
  3. Blue lines and NEXT tags show where a box goes. Green lines and FROM tags show where it comes from. Everything else fades.
  4. + opens a box's next steps, and − folds them away. ✓ Yes / Approve labels are green; ✗ No / Reject labels are red.
  5. ▶ Walk goes through the flow one box at a time. ◎ Focus hides everything except the box and its direct links.
  6. ← Back returns to the last box. The path at the top shows where you are; tap any part of it to jump there.
  7. Close details by tapping an empty part of the map, pressing ✕ or using Show / Hide details. Drag to move; pinch or Ctrl + scroll to zoom; tap the mini-map to jump.
  8. On a phone, ☰ Tools holds search, roles and the buttons. It hides itself while you use the map.
